Package index

Running an optimization

One generic for every algorithm. Which of the three shapes the objective arrived in is settled separately, so an algorithm is written once.

minimize()
Minimize a Function
maximize()
Maximize a Function
optimizer_result()
S7 Class for the Result of an Optimization

Smooth problems

Methods that build a model of the surface from derivatives. Fast when the objective is smooth, and misled when it is not.

newton()
Newton's Method with a Modified Hessian
bfgs()
BFGS
lbfgs()
Limited-Memory BFGS
cg()
Nonlinear Conjugate Gradients
bb()
The Barzilai-Borwein Method
gd()
Gradient Descent

Noisy and large problems

Adam, which tolerates a gradient that points downhill only on average. It draws no minibatches of its own: an objective that resamples is a closure, written by the caller, who knows what an observation is.

adam()
Adaptive Moment Estimation

Problems with a kink

Where a descent method arrives at the answer and cannot certify it, because the subgradient it evaluates never becomes small.

bundle()
The Proximal Bundle Method
prox_grad()
Proximal Gradient Method
nelder_mead()
The Nelder-Mead Simplex Method
compass()
Pattern Search, With Coordinate or Random Polling

Searching before descending

A global search for the problems where the answer depends on which basin the run began in. It is meant to hand its result to a local method rather than to finish the job itself.

sa()
Simulated Annealing With an Adaptive Step

Wrapping an optimizer

Both are themselves optimizers, so they compose with everything above and with each other. Multi-start reports what a single run cannot, the number of distinct optima; a chain runs its stages in order, each starting where the previous finished.

multistart()
Run an Optimizer From Many Starting Points
chain()
Run Optimizers One After Another

Stopping rules

A criterion is an object implementing one generic, so a user-defined rule is treated like a shipped one. An optimizer rejects a rule it cannot evaluate rather than accepting one that never fires.

criterion()
S7 Class for Convergence Criteria
crit_met()
Has the Stopping Rule Been Met?
crit_needs()
What a Criterion Needs From the Iteration
crit_grad()
Stop When the Gradient Is Small
crit_abs_obj()
Stop When the Objective Stops Moving (Absolute)
crit_rel_obj()
Stop When the Objective Stops Moving (Relative)
crit_abs_par()
Stop When the Parameters Stop Moving (Absolute)
crit_rel_par()
Stop When the Parameters Stop Moving (Relative)
crit_stationary()
Stop When the Method's Own Measure of Progress Is Small
crit_never()
Never Stop Early
crit_any()
Stop When Any of Several Rules Fires
crit_all()
Stop Only When Every Rule Fires

Line searches

How far to go along a direction, once the direction is chosen. The non-monotone rule is not an exotic option: a method whose step length is itself the method, as Barzilai-Borwein’s is, needs a search that does not reshape it.

line_search()
S7 Class for Line Searches
armijo()
Backtracking Line Search with the Armijo Condition
wolfe()
Line Search Satisfying the Strong Wolfe Conditions
nonmonotone()
Nonmonotone Backtracking

Starting values

A starter stands in for the vector of starting values, and is resolved on the unconstrained scale, so a single constant means something sensible for every kind of parameter and no draw can land outside its bounds.

start_zeros()
Start From Zero on the Unconstrained Scale
start_runif()
Start From a Uniform Draw on the Unconstrained Scale
starting_values()
Produce a Vector of Starting Values
infer_npar()
How Many Parameters the Objective Takes

The objective

A function of the parameter vector. The generic is the extension point: a caller with its own kind of objective registers one method and every algorithm accepts it.

as_objective()
Normalize an Objective for the Optimizers

Writing an optimizer of your own

What a minimize() method of your own has to promise, and the pieces that let it. check_optimizer() tests the contract; the battery under it reports the power; they are separate because they are different questions.
